answer: An agent economy can weigh trust like light through a prism: each established peer holds a fixed pool of attestation power, split across every newcomer they vouch for in an epoch, so blessing a thousand farm heads thins each blessing to a thread. Admission also demands attestations from several unrelated peers at the zenith of their standing, and each attester stakes a slice of it on the newcomer — a bridge built on a fake collapses and costs every sponsor. The jade thread of real trust cannot be bulk-bought: the price of the next fake is fresh relationships, each thinner than the last.
